subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Describe a photo for about one minute in clear stages.
Use phrases like 'This photo shows ...' and 'in the background'.
Guess with might, I think and I guess, and give reasons.

tf.s: Fluency means speaking with few pauses and little repetition.
We can start a photo description with 'This photo shows ...'.
tf.why: It introduces the main idea of the photo.

tf.s: We use 'might' when we are completely sure.
The study tip suggests about 15 seconds for each stage of the description.
tf.why: Four stages of 15 seconds make one minute.

tf.s: A good description only names the objects in the photo.
tf.why: You should also describe the place, the people and their actions.

tf.s: 'In the background' describes things behind the main people.
tf.why: For example: In the background there are some trees.

tf.s: We say 'This photo was taken in a bus'.

tf.why: For example: They're definitely at home.

tf.s: You should stop talking after 15 seconds in the one-minute long turn.
tf.why: Try to speak for the full minute.

tf.s: Talking about people's clothes is a good way to fill one minute.
tf.why: Appearance and clothes add useful details.

boxes.why: It tells the listener what the photo is about.

boxes.q: Complete: In the ___, there are some trees and buildings.
boxes.why: Things behind the main people are in the background.

boxes.q: Complete: This photo was taken ___ a bus.
Which word shows you are sure?
How long is the individual long turn?
boxes.why: You describe the photo for about one minute.

boxes.q: Which sentence says where the photo was taken?
Complete: The boy ___ the left has short hair.
What does 'The boys are both wearing coats' describe?
You are not sure. Complete: ___ they're at a party.
boxes.why: 'I guess' shows you are not sure.

mcq.q: What are the four stages of a one-minute photo description?
o: Introduce the idea, describe the place, the people's appearance, what they are doing
mcq.why: Following stages keeps your description organised.

mcq.q: Why do we say 'The friends might be watching a film'?
Which question words help you plan to speak for thirty seconds?
mcq.why: These questions give you ideas to talk about.

mcq.q: Which phrase introduces your opinion or guess?
Improve: 'They are at home. They eat pizza.'
o: They're definitely at home because there's a sofa, and they're eating pizza together.
They are at home at home.
They ate pizza at home tomorrow.
mcq.why: Reasons and the present continuous make it better.

mcq.q: Photo: three girls on a sofa with a laptop. Which sentence describes the action?
o: They're looking at a laptop together.
This photo shows a typical scene.
In the background there's a window.
The girl on the left has long hair.

mcq.q: Choose the correct order: photo / a typical scene / shows / this / in a supermarket
o: This photo shows a typical scene in a supermarket.
This shows photo a typical scene in a supermarket.
A typical scene this photo shows in a supermarket.
In a supermarket shows this photo a typical scene.

mcq.q: A student stops after 30 seconds. What could they add to fill one minute?
o: People's appearance, clothes, more objects and the background
mcq.why: More details help you speak for the full minute.

mcq.q: Which sentence gives a guess with a reason?
o: I think they are sisters because they look similar.
mcq.why: 'I think' shows the guess and 'because' gives the reason.

mcq.q: Why is it useful to organise a photo description into stages?
o: It helps you speak fluently and not forget ideas
It means you don't need to look at the photo
It stops you from using adjectives
mcq.why: A clear plan makes speaking easier.
